new_camps.name: Jerry Lakes basin camp
new_camps.why: Open basin beside the Jerry Lakes with water close by. Summit day drops into the next basin before climbing to the ridge near 7,200 ft, so leave before dawn.
new_camps.water: Jerry Lakes and snowmelt in the basin.
new_camps.notes: Reached by crossing the high pass beside Crater Mountain and descending snow below the Jerry Glacier; roughly 9 miles and 5,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The 6,000 ft figure is for the basin west of the lakes where parties pitch tents.

camps.name: May Creek Camp, Ross Lake
camps.why: Last designated camp on the East Bank Trail. The off-trail climb to the Nohokomeen Glacier starts in the woods just above it, so one tent serves both nights.

plan_conflict: The plan returns to camp after the summit, but one party descended the East Ridge and left by the Jerry Glacier side instead of walking back to May Creek.

camps.name: Camp on the east side of Jack
camps.why: Basin camp near 6,000 ft past the Jerry Glacier crossing, with the pass behind you. The glacier summit day starts and ends here, so it serves both nights.

new_camps.name: Jerry Lakes basin camp
new_camps.why: Basin at the Jerry Lakes with water at hand, a short climb from the 7,200 ft step where the southeast ridge begins. Holds the tent for both nights.
new_camps.water: Jerry Lakes and snowmelt in the basin.
new_camps.notes: Reached from Crater Lake over the Crater Mountain saddle and across the Jerry Glacier. A party camped two nights in the 6,000 ft basin west of the lakes and climbed the southeast ridge from there.

plan_conflict: The plan mentions a Crater Creek camp as an alternative; a party that stopped at Crater Creek Meadows on the way never reached the lakes basin that trip.

camps.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps.why: Short, steep walk-in above the trailhead; fine for a night before. The climb itself needs a bivy high on the face, which is not part of this camp.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 at a high bivy near the base of the northeast face; sources found place the bivy near 7,100 ft for the 1951 rib, not this line, so night 1 is unconfirmed.

camps.name: Head of Kindy Creek and the Kindy-Buck Creek pass
camps.why: Basins near the head of Kindy Creek put the glacier summit day within one round trip of the tent, at the end of a long off-trail approach.

camps.name: Horse Lake saddle camp
camps.why: Stopping place on the Green Mountain approach, with slow sidehill still ahead. Not a base for the summit day on this Kindy Ridge plan.

plan_conflict: No trip report found that names where parties sleep on this approach; camps come from the plan and the camps on file.

camps.name: Jug Lake
camps.why: Lower, brushier lake base at about 3,900 ft. It makes the summit day far longer than camping on the heather benches above, so most parties skip it.

new_camps.name: Heather bench camp below the west face
new_camps.why: Flat heather ground near 6,000 ft below the west ramp. Camping here makes the summit a short day and avoids a huge car-to-car push through the brush.
new_camps.notes: Other flat spots are reported near 5,600 ft on the ridge south-southwest of Point 6356 and just west of the summit near 6,500 ft. Cliff Lake is buggy and less liked for camping.

plan_conflict: The camp on file, Jug Lake, is not where the plan sleeps; the plan's night 1 is the heather bench near 6,000 ft.

camps.name: Bench bivy below Megalodon Ridge
camps.why: Exposed bench below the technical climbing, reached after a short fifth-class step. Little room, but the full ridge starts fresh the next morning.

camps.name: Fireweed Camp, Bridge Creek / PCT
camps.why: Overflow choice on the PCT when the North Fork camps are full. Leaves a much bigger day to the ridge and is not slept at on a normal trip.

camps.name: North Fork Camp, Bridge Creek / PCT junction
camps.why: Natural stop if you start late from the trailhead. It adds a long day before the brushy off-trail approach, so most parties continue to the bench.

camps.name: Walker Park Camp
camps.why: First camp that shortens the walk toward the Goode Glacier drainage. Parties continuing to the bench bivy pass it by.

new_camps.name: Summit bivy, Mount Goode
new_camps.why: The ridge takes a full day, so parties reach the top near sunset and sleep there, then descend in daylight. Cold and exposed, with ledges for a few people.
new_camps.notes: Ledges at the top are reported to fit about four people, with two more a short way below.

plan_conflict: Night 3 (the descent toward Park Creek) has no camp that could be placed with an elevation; nights 1 and 2 are well supported.

camps.name: Valley bivy below the buttress
camps.why: Classic first night near 5,200 to 5,500 ft at the base of the cliffs below the glacier. A bench with room for a tent or two; the climb starts a short walk away.

camps.name: Goode Glacier moraine
camps.why: Higher option that shortens the climbing day, but the carry up is rough and the ground is limited. Choose it for the earliest start.

camps.name: Summit bivy
camps.why: The buttress takes about nine hours, so most parties top out late and sleep on the summit, then descend in daylight. Cold and exposed, with a few ledges.

plan_conflict: Summit bivy is the main camp on night 2, not a route option; night 3 (the descent) has no camp that could be placed with an elevation, and parties differ on whether they camp or walk out.

camps.name: Klawatti Col camp, Eldorado ice-cap traverse approach
camps.why: Col between the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers near 7,800 ft: windy and shelterless, but Primus is a short glacier day away so parties stay put here.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 at an Eldorado high camp, but parties reported reaching the col camp on day 1 and staying there for the summit day.

camps.name: Rib camp below Storm King/Goode basin
camps.why: Flat grassy rib near 7,400 ft just south of Storm King with water close. The summit cirque is right above, so the climb is one day from the tent.

camps.name: Neve Camp
camps.why: Low forest camp near the Thunder Creek trailhead on the west-side approach. Not on this Stehekin boat-and-bus plan.

camps.name: Junction Camp
camps.why: Thunder Creek trail camp ten miles in on the west-side approach over Park Creek Pass. Far from this plan's route.

camps.name: Skagit Queen Camp
camps.why: Last creekside camp on the Thunder Creek side before the headwaters. West-side approach only; not used on this plan.

camps.name: Thunder Basin Hiker Camp
camps.why: Meadow camp on the west side of Park Creek Pass, a staging point for the neighbouring peaks. Not on the Stehekin approach.

camps.name: Five Mile Camp, Park Creek trail
camps.why: Creekside Park Creek camp set aside for stock. It lies below the plan's first stop, so it is only a fallback.

plan_conflict: Night 1 (the plan's Two Mile Camp) could not be confirmed or given an elevation; the only party that reached the high rib did so in one long day, so nights are unconfirmed.

camps.name: Trapper Lake
camps.why: Lake water at the foot of the south slopes. The cost is a brushy off-trail descent from the Pelton Basin side, so day one is mostly spent reaching it.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp
camps.why: Camp at the end of the old upper Stehekin road on the east side. It is for a different approach and is not slept at on the Cascade Pass plan.

plan_conflict: No trip report found that names where parties sleep for a South Slopes climb; the camp comes from the plan.

new_camps.name: Glacier toe bivy, Davis Peak north face
new_camps.why: Flat snow at the toe of the glacier with running water, an hour below the bergschrund. Cold, and the day in is a long bushwhack from the Stetattle Creek ford.
new_camps.notes: Reached by fording Stetattle Creek and scrambling a rib through slide alder. A winter party kicked out bivy sites on the snow.

camps.name: Graybeal Camp
camps.why: Closest established camp to Indian Mountain, up Brush Creek. The summit day starts and ends here, so one tent serves both nights. Often dry; fill bottles before arriving.

camps.name: Hannegan Camp, below Hannegan Pass
camps.why: Staging camp on the forest side of the pass for a late arrival. It leaves a much longer second day to the Brush Creek camp.

camps.name: Boundary Camp
camps.why: A few sites just over Hannegan Pass in the park, needing a park permit. It shortens day two but is not a base for the summit.

camps.name: US Cabin Camp, Chilliwack River
camps.why: Deep-forest valley camp on the Chilliwack, a stop for parties heading to peaks further up the drainage. Short of Brush Creek.

plan_conflict: No trip report found that names where parties sleep for Indian Mountain; the camp comes from the plan.

camps.name: Thornton Pass (camp knob)
camps.why: Benched ground on the Thornton Ridge crest after the long brushy climb. The camp-to-camp summit day starts and ends here.

camps.name: Upper Despair Lake
camps.why: Not a documented camp. It is the last reliable water before the cliff band, and an emergency stop if the long day runs dark.

plan_conflict: One report of the approach camps at Triumph Pass instead of Thornton Pass; no report confirms where Despair parties on this plan sleep.
No report found for this route's nights; the plan's rocky knob camp near 6,100 ft south of Thornton Pass has no researched elevation, so none is added.

camps.name: Whatcom Camp, Brush Creek below Whatcom Pass
camps.why: Last trail camp below the pass, with water. Night before the glacier crossing on the way in and first sleep back on the way out.

camps.name: Luna Cirque high camp (near Lousy Lake)
camps.why: High camp on the Luna side reached from Big Beaver. It belongs to the other approach, not this Hannegan Pass plan.

camps.name: Perfect Pass, Perfect Pass cross-country zone
camps.why: Benches by the Challenger Glacier at 6,300 ft; a high camp for the neighbouring peaks. This plan crosses it to a camp further on.

camps.name: Improvised bivouacs on the Challenger Glacier and the crest south of Challenger
camps.why: Nights out on the ice for parties far down the chain; not planned on this trip.

plan_conflict: Nights 1, 3 and 4 could not be confirmed: one party reports a bivy under Ghost Peak after crossing Perfect Pass, but no elevation or name for the high camp.

new_camps.name: Access Creek Basin
new_camps.why: Where the Access Creek bushwhack ends, with creek water. It leaves a manageable climb to Access Col the next morning.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the Big Beaver Trail and a brushy bushwhack. Parties report camping in the upper basin beside a large boulder.

new_camps.name: Luna Col (Luna Pass)
new_camps.why: Windy col with little flat ground; parties camp here after Access Col and again after the climb. It saves re-crossing the pass on summit day.
new_camps.notes: Used as a camp by parties on the nearby southeast glacier route as well.

new_camps.name: Luna Cirque camp
new_camps.why: Flat, sandy ground in the cirque directly below the North Buttress, so the pre-dawn start is short; the cost is a 2,400 ft descent and re-climb to Luna Col.
new_camps.water: A creek about eight minutes west of the camp.

plan_conflict: Night 4 is unconfirmed: one party instead spent several nights on the summit, and the plan itself allows a high bivouac.

camps.name: Access Creek headwaters basin
camps.why: Open basin above the bushwhack with creek water; the usual first night before Access Col.

camps.name: East Fury summit bivy
camps.why: Flat rock on East Fury at the jumping-off point for the ridge; a bivy sack can stay standing for the return.

camps.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
camps.why: Trail camp short of the Access Creek bushwhack. Choose it for an easier first day, at the price of a longer day two.

camps.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
camps.why: Open ground on the col above Luna Cirque, the working camp after West Fury and the last sleep before the walk out.

new_camps.name: Glacier moat bivy below the upper ridge
new_camps.why: A small glacier on the south side of the upper ridge offers a moat to shelter in, about 500 ft below West Fury's top. Reached after dark by slow parties.
new_camps.notes: One solo climber slept in the moat between ice and rock near the end of the ridge.

plan_conflict: Night 3 (first gendarmes) has no sourced camp, and the one solo report fits the ridge into fewer nights than the plan.
